content: Azithromycin and flecainide both prolong the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Azithromycin and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring is advised, and caution should be exercised. Azithromycin and fluoxetine both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin and fluphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the effects of fondaparinux by reducing its metabolism. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Azithromycin and formoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and foscarnet both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. Azithromycin and gadobenate both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of gemifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and gepirone both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Azithromycin and gilteritinib both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Azithromycin and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. Azithromycin and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc prolongation. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Goserelin increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Azithromycin and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Azithromycin and haloperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the effects of heparin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Histrelin increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Azithromycin and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Azithromycin and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Azithromycin and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin and imipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and indacaterol (inhaled) both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that are known to prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Azithromycin and indapamide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of indinavir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and inotuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiation of any QTc-prolonging drug, and periodically monitor as clinically indicated during treatment. Azithromycin and isoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of isradipine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and lapatinib both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin and lefamulin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Azithromycin and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Azithromycin and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of azithromycin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Azithromycin and levoketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and lithium both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Azithromycin and lofepramine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of lofexidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of loratadine via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and macimorelin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Macimorelin causes an increase of approximately 11 milliseconds in the corrected QT interval. Avoid coadministration with drugs that prolong the QT interval, as this could increase the risk of torsades de pointes-type ventricular tachycardia. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. Azithromycin and maprotiline both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and mavorixafor both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation (e.g., coadministered medications that increase mavorixafor exposure or other drugs with a high risk of QTc prolongation). Dose reduction or discontinuation of mavorixafor may be required. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of mefloquine by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Azithromycin and methadone both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin decreases the effects of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Oral microbiota contains bacterial spores, and antibacterial agents may decrease efficacy if coadministered. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota. Azithromycin and mifepristone both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Use alternatives if available. Azithromycin and mirtazapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Azithromycin and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin decreases the effects of nafcillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. Azithromycin increases the levels of naldemedine via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor naldemedine for potential adverse effects if coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. Azithromycin and nilotinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the levels of nintedanib via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If adverse effects occur, management may require interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation of therapy. Azithromycin and nortriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and octreotide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of olanzapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and olodaterol (inhaled) both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the effects of beta-2 agonists on the cardiovascular system, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Azithromycin and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid use in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended with concomitant medications that prolong the QT interval, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. Azithromycin and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and osimertinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Conduct periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. Azithromycin decreases the effects of oxacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of oxaliplatin. Use caution and monitor closely. Both oxaliplatin and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Azithromycin and ozanimod both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. Azithromycin and paliperidone both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat is known to significantly prolong the QT interval. Panobinostat prescribing information states that use with drugs known to prolong QTc is not recommended. Azithromycin decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Azithromycin and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin decreases the effects of penicillin G aqueous by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin decreases the effects of penicillin VK by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Azithromycin and perphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the effects of phenindione by reducing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of pimavanserin by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of pimozide by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Both azithromycin and pimozide prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Azithromycin decreases the effects of piperacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of pitolisant by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin increases the levels of pomalidomide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Azithromycin and posaconazole both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Azithromycin and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Azithromycin and procainamide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Azithromycin and prochlorperazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and promazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and promethazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of propafenone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the effects of protamine by reducing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Azithromycin and protriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin and quetiapine both increase each other’s toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for QT prolongation.
